svg.text: A cell becomes a sorted sentence of gene names.
Magnitudes are discarded; only relative rank is kept. The result is a token sequence a BERT-style encoder can mask and predict.

g.text: ~19 000 gene counts from one cell · mostly zeros
cell.X = one row of the count matrix
• protocol differences shift the absolute scale
A naïve BERT over this vector would spend
most of its attention on zeros.
Rank by expression within this cell
truncated to the model's context length
A gene at rank 2 is "more important to
this cell" than a gene at rank 8 —
regardless of the actual UMI count.
CD3E at rank 2 in cell A and at rank 2
in cell B carries the same signal,
the ranked list is fed to a BERT encoder
bidirectional self-attention over the ranked gene tokens
treats a cell like a sentence
• a fixed-length sequence of gene tokens
position in the sequence is the magnitude
Identical to NLP from here on:
"the genes this cell expresses, in order"
Vocabulary differs; mechanics are the same.
classic masked language modeling, gene-vocab edition
For the first [MASK] the model predicts:
• which genes co-occur at similar ranks
• which gene sets identify each cell type
All of it without ever seeing a UMI count.
Magnitude is discarded. Only relative rank
matters. This is what makes the encoding
differences — and what lets a single model
(at the cost of throwing away signal where magnitude actually matters)
